clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old male presented to cardiology on November 3, 2021 with palpitations, nocturnal bilateral calf leg cramps, fatigue, dizziness, and loss of balance. He was on chronic medications including amlodipine, aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and prednisone, suggesting prior cardiovascular risk factors. Orthostatic hypotension was ruled out. He had prior evaluation by PCP and ENT for vertigo. Cardiac catheterization/angiography performed on 10/03/23 revealed moderate disease of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery, occlusion of the left vertebral artery at its ostium, severe stenosis of 80-90% in the right vertebral artery at the proximal segment, and an ejection fraction of 55-60%. Brain MRI on 11/09/23 showed generalized cerebral atrophy with normal brain structures, no acute cerebrovascular accident, no mass, and no bleeding. On 08/16/23 follow-up, the patient reported worsening episodes of dizziness, loss of balance, and fatigue, consistent with vertebrobasilar insufficiency from the identified vertebral artery disease.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with palpitations, nocturnal bilateral calf leg cramps, fatigue, dizziness, and loss of balance
Orthostatic hypotension was ruled out at presentation
Patient was on amlodipine, aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and prednisone at presentation, indicating prior cardiovascular disease management

Angiographic results on 10/03/23 revealed moderate disease of the LAD artery, occlusion of the left vertebral artery at its ostium, severe stenosis of 80-90% in the right vertebral artery at the proximal segment, and EF of 55-60%
Brain MRI on 11/09/23 showed generalized cerebral atrophy with normal brain structures, no acute CVA, no mass, no bleeding, and no abnormal enhancement
On 08/16/23 follow-up, patient reported worsening episodes of dizziness, loss of balance, and fatigue

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Brain MRI on 11/09/23 showed no acute CVA, no bleeding, no mass lesion, and normal diffusion signal

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Orthostatic hypotension as cause of dizziness and balance loss
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Orthostatic hypotension was explicitly ruled out at initial presentation (E001)
Ejection fraction was preserved at 55-60%, not reduced

remaining_uncertainties: Specific indication for cardiac catheterization on 10/03/23 (what ECG or clinical findings prompted the procedure)
ECG findings at initial presentation on November 3, 2021
Cardiac examination findings (heart rate, rhythm character) at presentation
Method of ejection fraction measurement (echocardiography vs cardiac MRI vs other modality) and specific date
Whether vertebral artery findings were incidentally discovered during cardiac angiography (with aortic arch imaging) or via dedicated cerebrovascular angiography
Treatment decisions and interventions following angiography (whether PCI/stenting was performed for LAD stenosis, anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy for vertebral artery disease)
Neurological examination findings at initial presentation
Prior medical history and documented diagnoses (hypertension, prior CAD, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, prior CVA/TIA)
Clinical response to treatment and long-term outcome
